content.comment_body: Hello everyone, today my [product_name] operator panel displayed the attached message, while the backlight cycled through orange, red, and white colors. The only way to stop it was to disconnect the power supply. After restoring power, the panel worked normally again. What does this event mean?
It sounds like there may be a hardware defect. I recommend initiating a support request.

The backlight colors of the [product_name] operator panel can be set in your program using specific markers, such as M26, M30, and M31. If you're not using these markers and still see the backlight changing colors, it's likely the device is defective. As a tip, using the keys on the panel sets the orange backlight briefly to improve visibility, but consecutive color cycling (orange-red-white) is not a normal feature.

analysis.insight_summary: Users described an unexpected issue with a [product_name] operator panel where the backlight cycled through multiple colors and displayed a message. Power cycling restored normal operation. Support responses clarified normal backlight functionality and suggested the device may be experiencing a hardware fault, as the observed behavior is not standard.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the operator panel backlight to operate consistently, with color changes occurring only as documented or through intended program logic.
